questions.questionContent: What is the primary purpose of a large-scale version control system like Piper?
options: To manage small codebases for individual developers
To handle massive codebases with thousands of developers
To replace Git in all scenarios
To provide a graphical user interface for version control
questions.correctAnswer: To handle massive codebases with thousands of developers

questions.questionContent: What is a key difference between Piper and Git?
options: Piper is centralized, while Git is distributed
Piper is open-source, while Git is proprietary
questions.correctAnswer: Piper is centralized, while Git is distributed

questions.questionContent: What is a 'monorepo' in the context of large-scale version control?
options: A single repository containing all code for an organization
A repository that only contains documentation
A repository that uses multiple version control systems
A repository that is only accessible to a single developer
questions.correctAnswer: A single repository containing all code for an organization

questions.questionContent: Why does Google use a monorepo for its codebase?
options: To simplify dependency management and code sharing
questions.correctAnswer: To simplify dependency management and code sharing

questions.questionContent: What is 'CitC' (Clients in the Cloud) in the context of Piper?
options: A feature that allows developers to work on code directly in the cloud
A tool for managing Git repositories
A type of merge conflict resolution
A backup system for version control
questions.correctAnswer: A feature that allows developers to work on code directly in the cloud

questions.questionContent: How does Piper handle branching compared to Git?
options: Piper uses lightweight branching with virtual workspaces
Piper does not support branching at all
Piper requires manual branch creation for every change
Piper uses the same branching model as Git
questions.correctAnswer: Piper uses lightweight branching with virtual workspaces

questions.questionContent: What is a 'virtual workspace' in Piper?
options: A lightweight, isolated environment for making changes
A tool for visualizing Git history
A backup of the entire codebase
questions.correctAnswer: A lightweight, isolated environment for making changes

questions.questionContent: What is the role of 'code review' in a Piper-like system?
options: To ensure code quality and enforce standards
To slow down the development process
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure code quality and enforce standards

questions.questionContent: What is 'trunk-based development' in the context of Piper?
options: A development model where all changes are committed to a single main branch
A model where each developer works in isolation
A model that avoids using branches entirely
A model that relies on long-lived feature branches
questions.correctAnswer: A development model where all changes are committed to a single main branch

questions.questionContent: How does Piper handle large binary files?
options: By using a separate storage system for binaries
By storing them directly in the repository
By converting them to text files
questions.correctAnswer: By using a separate storage system for binaries

questions.questionContent: What is 'dependency management' in a monorepo?
options: The process of managing relationships between different parts of the codebase
The process of deleting unused code
The process of creating new branches
The process of merging code from different repositories
questions.correctAnswer: The process of managing relationships between different parts of the codebase

questions.questionContent: What is 'atomic commit' in the context of Piper?
options: A commit that includes all related changes as a single unit
A commit that only includes one file
A commit that is automatically reverted
A commit that is not reviewed
questions.correctAnswer: A commit that includes all related changes as a single unit

questions.questionContent: What is 'code visibility' in a Piper-like system?
options: The ability to see and access code across the entire organization
The ability to hide code from other developers
The ability to delete code permanently
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to see and access code across the entire organization

questions.questionContent: What is 'pre-submit testing' in Piper?
options: Running tests before code is submitted to the main branch
Running tests after code is merged
Running tests only on the developer's machine
questions.correctAnswer: Running tests before code is submitted to the main branch

questions.questionContent: What is 'post-submit testing' in Piper?
options: Running tests after code is merged into the main branch
Running tests before code is submitted
Running tests only on the developer's machine
questions.correctAnswer: Running tests after code is merged into the main branch

questions.questionContent: What is 'code search' in the context of a monorepo?
options: A tool for finding code across the entire repository
A tool for creating new repositories
questions.correctAnswer: A tool for finding code across the entire repository

questions.questionContent: What is 'code ownership' in a Piper-like system?
options: A system for assigning responsibility for specific parts of the codebase
A system for creating new repositories
questions.correctAnswer: A system for assigning responsibility for specific parts of the codebase

questions.questionContent: What is 'continuous integration' in the context of Piper?
options: Automatically integrating and testing changes as they are made
Manually integrating changes after they are reviewed
questions.correctAnswer: Automatically integrating and testing changes as they are made

questions.questionContent: What is 'continuous deployment' in the context of Piper?
options: Automatically deploying changes to production after they pass tests
Manually deploying changes after they are reviewed
questions.correctAnswer: Automatically deploying changes to production after they pass tests

questions.questionContent: What is 'scalability' in the context of a version control system?
options: The ability to handle a growing number of developers and code
The ability to create new repositories
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to handle a growing number of developers and code

questions.questionContent: What is 'fault tolerance' in the context of Piper?
options: The ability to continue operating despite hardware or software failures
The ability to create new repositories
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to continue operating despite hardware or software failures

questions.questionContent: What is 'data consistency' in the context of a version control system?

questions.correctAnswer: Ensuring that all copies of the codebase are identical

questions.questionContent: What is 'distributed caching' in the context of Piper?

questions.questionContent: What is 'load balancing' in the context of Piper?
